Chapter 2: Discovering the ‘Little Way’—Simplicity, Trust, and the Path to Holiness
Think back to those teenage years, when suddenly, everything just feels... more complicated. Expectations grow, and trying to be good can start to feel like a battle you’re destined to lose. There are moments when patience runs thin, or a tiny slight leaves you fighting back tears. But even in those tough moments, something deeper starts to take root. The longing for God isn’t just a feeling anymore—it’s slowly becoming a way of living.
You might think holiness is only for the extraordinary—the saints whose stories glow in stained glass, or heroes who do incredible things. But for one young woman, the journey to God unfolded in the most ordinary ways. She began to notice that true greatness isn’t about grand gestures, but about doing the small things, the everyday things, with real love. This realization didn’t strike her all at once. It grew quietly, through stumbles and setbacks, through gentle encouragement and silent moments of doubt.
Picture her: one evening, feeling defeated after a hard day, sitting alone and reflecting on all the ways she’d fallen short. The urge to just give up was strong. And then, a thought surfaced—almost like a whisper. What if God isn’t looking for perfection? What if even the smallest, honest effort is enough? That idea brought a sense of freedom she hadn’t felt before. She realized she didn’t have to impress anyone or chase after big achievements. All she needed to do was love in the present moment—maybe by offering a smile to a difficult sister, sharing a kind word with a stranger, or just bearing a small discomfort without complaining.
This became the heart of what’s called the ‘Little Way.’ It isn’t a checklist or a complicated spiritual program. It’s more like a new lens for seeing the world, trusting that every small act, if done with love, matters. The ‘Little Way’ is grounded in humility—knowing that our efforts are limited, but believing God’s grace can fill in the gaps. And it’s about trust—a childlike confidence that God will provide, even when you can’t see what’s ahead.
Of course, not everyone got it. Some people thought this approach was a little too simple, maybe even naïve. But for those who gave it a try, the change was real. The heavy burden of trying to prove yourself started to lift, replaced by a quiet kind of joy. Suddenly, even the most boring tasks became chances to serve. And when hard times came, instead of growing bitter, they found a way to draw closer to God.
One day, while she was helping out with chores, she noticed something: it’s easy to feel annoyed when your hard work goes unnoticed. The desire for recognition is strong, isn’t it? But then, she remembered the ‘Little Way’—how hidden sacrifices are often the most meaningful. So, she decided to keep working quietly, offering it all up in silence, trusting that God saw what others didn’t. The peace she felt after making that choice was unmistakable.
Over time, this simple approach didn’t just change her—it changed the people around her, too. The ‘Little Way’ became a source of hope for anyone who ever felt too small or too weak to make a difference. It’s a reminder that holiness isn’t about being noticed. It’s about loving well, right where you are, in the middle of everyday life. Most of us overlook the power of small acts, but in this story, it’s clear—the path to God is often found in the simplest things.
